full_judgment:
18. Mr Md Lutfor Rahman Mondal, the learned Advocate for the opposite party on appearing before this Court, on the other hand, submitted that in view of section 101 of the Evidence Act, the burden of proof of the pleadings case cannot be shifted. He further submitted that the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1992 came up before the Court with a specific pleadings but they failed to discharge their onus as per law. He further submitted that the Title Suit No. 23 of 1992 was filed during life time of Soleman and he died long after four years of filing of the suit but said Soleman did not make any attempt to compare the LTI as contained in the back of page No 1 of Exhibit 1 with his admitted LTI. He further submitted that no prayer was made by Soleman for making a comparison of the signature of LTI as contained in Exhibit 1 with his admitted signature and LTI to prove that the Exhibit 1 was not executed by Soleman. He further submitted that the Exhibit 1 was admitted into evidence and was marked as Exhibit 1 without having any objection from the defendant side. He further submitted that the Exhibit 1 being a registered instrument that carries a presumption of correctness and validity. In support of his contention he relied upon the case law reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 150 and the case of Abdullah and 3 others vs Abdul Hakim and others, reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205. He further submitted that the execution of Soleman has been proved beyond doubt by the plaintiff by adducing the evidence of PW 1 and PW 2 who corroborated each other. Mr Mondal submitted that the impugned judgment and decree being the judgment of affirmance there is nothing to interfere by this Court unless a strong case of no consideration of any evidence or no reading of any evidence or misreading of any evidence on record is made out. He relied upon the case law of Azifannessa vs Sakur Miah and others, reported in 30 DLR (AD) 41. He lastly submitted that the Exhibit 1 being a registered document and having been exhibited without any objection, the same shall be presumed to be correct and valid. In support of his contention he relied upon the decision reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 114. 

 19. On perusal of the case law reported in 1993 BLD (AD) 114 it appears that our Appellate Division has held that the presumption of correctness of a Registered Document is a rebut table presumption and after giving due opportunity to the parties concerned the same can be rebutted. So, that decision goes against Mr Mondal. The presumption of correctness is not conclusive. On perusal of the Case law reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205 it appears that objection as to formal proof of document to be taken at earliest point of time. Here in the instant case the document Exhibit 1 itself is the questioned document. Its formal proof although was not objected initially but the very deed having classified to be a forged one, the defendant will not be debarred from questioning the validity of that deed. That decision does not apply in the instant suit. 

 20. In reply Mr Mohammad Habibullah, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that the presumption of correctness of a registered documents does not carry any evidentiary value of correctness. He submitted that the presumption is always rebut table and he relied upon the decision reported in 7 BLR (AD) 306.
